title: P39: pretraining-only residual-branch dropout at 5%
description: P39: apply independent elementwise inverted dropout with probability 0.05 to the attention-output and MLP-output projections in all four blocks during pretraining only. Reducing reliance on co-adapted short-proof features may give fixed downstream expert iteration a policy that discovers and learns longer proofs more effectively.
hypothesis: Incumbent 043-codex scores 282/275/269 (exact mean 275.333333). No existing record tests P39 residual-branch dropout. Earlier label smoothing (017), EMA (025), z-loss (042), and late uniform averaging (048) failed against their respective incumbents, so generic regularization has weak evidence here. Unlike those mechanisms, branch dropout trains each token representation with randomly missing contributions inside every block while leaving the prediction objective and final handoff weights unchanged. This may reduce brittle co-adaptation to cap-6 proof patterns and improve round-1 discovery and subsequent compounding under fixed RL. It may instead damage precise proof features or cost useful updates within the fixed wall-clock budget. The mechanism is a hypothesis, not a diagnosed failure; only the fixed downstream three-seed mean decides keep/discard. This experiment is distinct from Claude ongoing 049 head-count change.
expected_delta: Conditional on improvement, +5 to +20 mean dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 over exact baseline mean 275.333333, with increased round-1 targets solved. Expect 1-8% fewer pretraining updates from eight dropout masks per forward/backward; no persistent RL/evaluation overhead. Pretraining train loss may rise and validation loss may improve without downstream gain; neither selects the outcome.

arch.dropout_scope: Pretraining training-mode residual branch outputs only, after proj and fc2 in each block, including projection bias. Independent elementwise masks with inverted scale 1/0.95; no attention-probability or embedding dropout. Evaluation/validation uses zero dropout and hooks are removed before RL.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 16 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of four blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding, readout, biases and LayerNorm retain their original draws/values. No reinitialization during RL.

regularization.name: residual-branch dropout
regularization.implementation: Eight removable forward hooks, one on each block.proj and block.fc2; F.dropout(..., training=module.training). Hooks registered after unchanged orthogonal initialization and removed unconditionally on normal loop exit before return. Frozen RL train() cannot reactivate them. No additional parameters or checkpoint keys.
regularization.rng: Uses normal global PyTorch RNG seeded by the frozen harness. Model initialization draws are unchanged; dropout advances global RNG during training. Separately seeded minibatch permutation/ref-shift generator and seed policy remain unchanged.
regularization.validation: model.eval() disables all masks during ordinary cross-entropy validation; model.train() reenables them until final hook removal.
